itinerary.text: Leave Ha Giang and follow the mountain roads towards Quan Ba. Pause at Bac Sum and the Twin Mountains viewpoints, then take a pine-hill break before continuing to Du Gia. The local team confirms the pine viewpoint and connecting road to suit the day's conditions and timing.

River access and pass viewpoints are sequenced locally to allow time for the descent and return. A boat trip is an option to confirm in the quote, not an automatic inclusion. Add a Skywalk viewpoint walk only when local access, weather and the group's ability allow; finish in Dong Van.

Continue to Dong Van for the proposed second night.

faqs.q: Should I choose the 3-day or 4-day Ha Giang Loop?
faqs.a: Both routes feature Du Gia, Nho Que River and Ma Pi Leng. The 3-day version returns on day three; the 4-day version adds a Lung Cu and northern-frontier day, plus a proposed third night in Yen Minh.

faqs.q: Is the Nho Que boat trip included?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Boat availability, tickets, transfer arrangements and inclusion in the price must be confirmed in your written quote.

faqs.q: Does the route cross the Chinese border?
faqs.a: No. The 4-day itinerary may include a locally permitted viewpoint on the Vietnam side. The exact stop is confirmed with the local team.

faqs.q: Which weaving village and return-day waterfall will we visit?
faqs.a: Lung Tam is the proposed weaving-village stop, subject to workshop access and route timing. The return-day waterfall location and feasibility must be confirmed with the team before booking.

faqs.q: How do I request a price and arrange transport?
faqs.a: Choose your itinerary and prepare your dates, group size and preferred travel style. Transport, rooms, meals and fees require written confirmation.
